title: Capacity Runway & Adaptive Autoscale Pilots for Dedicated Pools
creator: Marco Alvarez
body: Objective: deliver a tested set of adaptive autoscale pilots across three dedicated pool patterns (steady, spiky, and mixed) to build capacity runway semantics that reduce cost-per-token by 18-25% for predictable workloads while preserving latency SLOs. This ticket scopes the 12-week roadmap slice: definition of pilot configurations, experiment matrix, success metrics, rollout guardrails, and integration points with billing and the Console. Workstreams include: autoscale policy definitions (hedged warm pools, surge reservoirs), runtime hooks for graceful fallback to cheaper model variants, observability dashboards for token-level cost attribution, and operator runbooks for failure/recovery. Outcome: validated pilot artifacts (configs, canary playbook, dashboard queries), a cross-team decision on default autoscale profiles, and a deployment-ready runbook for Dedicated customers who opt into adaptive autoscale.
acceptance_criteria: Three pilot configurations (steady, spiky, mixed) deployed to staging Dedicated pools
Experiment matrix with hypothesis and sample size for each pilot documented in Confluence
Cost and latency baselines collected pre- and post-pilot with >95% confidence intervals
Canary rollback and automatic fallback to baseline capacity verified end-to-end
Console dashboard templates and alert thresholds created and reviewed by Observability team
Runbook covering common failure modes and manual remediation steps published and approved
milestones: Week 0-2: finalize pilot definitions, success metrics, and infra contracts (ENG signoff)
Week 3-6: implement autoscale policies and runtime telemetry hooks; deploy to staging
Week 7-9: run experiments, collect data, iterate on policy thresholds
Week 10-12: analyze results, prepare playbook, and propose default profiles for release

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: autoscale oscillation under mixed workloads could violate latency SLOs — Mitigation: conservative initial thresholds, smoothing window, and automatic fallback to pegged capacity
Risk: incorrect cost attribution could mislead decisions — Mitigation: tie telemetry to token-level billing IDs and run a parallel accounting query against Billing sandbox
Risk: customer confusion on new behavior — Mitigation: UI explainer, email pilot opt-in flow, and runtime toggle with clear revert path
metrics_and_okrs: OKR: Reduce median cost-per-token for steady bursts by 20% for pilot participants (KPI measured over 30-day window)
Latency: 95th percentile tail must not degrade more than 10% vs baseline under pilot conditions
Reliability: no increase in error rate >0.5% attributable to autoscale changes
Operational: Mean time to recover (MTTR) for autoscale regressions < 30 minutes with runbook
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal team-only pilot on a single Dedicated customer mirror (2 pools) — validate safety checks
Beta: invite 5 opt-in customers across three workload types; enable Console toggle and scheduled audit calls
GA gating: pass metrics thresholds for cost and latency plus documented runbook and automated rollback
Post-GA: enable default profile recommendation for new Dedicated customers and publish cost-savings case studies
